items.review_rationale: Read the set of prime ideals where the localized R-module M_p is nonzero, distinguishing module localization at p from localization of R or pointwise module annihilation.

references.context: Commutative algebra: multiplicative subset complementary to prime ideal used for localizing module M

references.disposition: The support membership test is nonvanishing of the localized module, not simply nonvanishing of M or annihilator of a single element.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed every-point and every-neighborhood quantification, requiring a quasi-compact neighborhood K of x contained in the prescribed neighborhood U, not merely local compactness in a Hausdorff sense.

references.phrase: neighborhood of a point in a topological space
references.context: Topology: subset containing an open set around the point, not necessarily open itself

references.phrase: for every neighborhood U of x
references.disposition: The quasi-compact K can depend on both x and U, and no ambient Hausdorff condition is asserted.

items.review_rationale: Read the full infinitesimal lifting condition for every R-algebra A and every square-zero ideal I, distinguishing existence of lifts from formal étaleness requiring uniqueness.

references.context: Commutative algebra: R-algebra with quotient by square-zero ideal and compatible R-algebra structure

references.phrase: lift of homomorphism S→A/I to S→A
references.context: Category theory and commutative algebra: diagonal lift in commuting square of R-algebra maps

references.phrase: I²=0 and every R-algebra map has a lift
references.disposition: Existence is the only requirement here; a unique lift is a stronger property and is not implied.

items.review_rationale: Read the maximal connected subset criterion under inclusion within ambient topological space X, which is not synonymous with a path component or arbitrary closed subset.

references.phrase: maximal under inclusion among connected subsets
references.context: Order theory: maximal element of family of connected subsets ordered by containment

references.disposition: Maximality is with respect to containing connected subsets, not maximum cardinality or an ambient openness assumption.

items.review_rationale: Read nonemptiness and both equivalent conditions: absence of separation into two nonempty open pieces and trivial clopen subsets. Kept the explicit nonempty convention rather than silently using the empty-is-connected convention.

references.context: Topology: subset simultaneously open and closed in the ambient space

references.phrase: disjoint decomposition into two nonempty open subsets
references.context: Topology: separation of a space by complementary disjoint nonempty open sets

references.disposition: The given formulation excludes the empty space from connectedness by its stated convention.

items.review_rationale: Read local connectedness as existence of a neighborhood basis consisting of connected neighborhoods around each point; mere existence of one connected neighborhood at each point is insufficient.

references.context: Topology: at each x, a family of connected neighborhoods refining every neighborhood of x

references.phrase: each point possesses a fundamental system
references.disposition: The system is required to refine arbitrary neighborhoods, not a single globally connected covering.

items.review_rationale: Read the pointwise statement that every connected component is a singleton, without identifying it with extremal disconnectedness, discrete topology, or failure of path-connectedness.

references.context: Set theory: one-element subset of X viewed as a connected component

references.disposition: The criterion does not require the topology to be discrete or all closures of open subsets to be open.

items.review_rationale: Read the group Aut(E/F) as field automorphisms of E fixing the embedded base field F pointwise, with composition law; distinguished it from arbitrary automorphisms of E and from the Galois-group property of special extensions.

references.context: Field theory: bijective field homomorphism from E to itself

references.disposition: The subgroup consists exactly of automorphisms fixing F pointwise, without requiring E/F to be Galois or finite.
